source.title: From Shallow to Deep: Pinning Semantic Intent via Causal GRPO
source.authors: Shu-Yi Zhou; Ze-En Song; Wen-Wen Qiang; Ji-Yan Sun; Yao Zhou; Yin-Long Liu; Weizhi Ma

record.tranche_reason: It reports harmful fine-tuning attack rates and evaluates prefix attacks, bearing on the claim, while its central intervention and representation measurements differ from the original shallow-alignment measurements.
record.gate_note: Table 2 reports the study's own fine-tuning attack outcomes. Section 4.1 reports a probe-accuracy collapse, not aligned-versus-base per-token KL. Table 1's detailed per-cell values are not used here because the extracted layout does not reliably map all cells to attack columns; the paper's explicit summary of those results is retained. Identity-shifting results are not included as evidence for harmful or ordinary benign fine-tuning: the training is designed to induce affirmative compliance.
record.test_reason: The study's own reproduced results bear on three versions. Its Standard SFT baseline repeats the original harmful-example attack (100 pairs, LLaMA-2-7B-Chat, protocol of Qi et al.) and bears on V1. Its reproduced prefill ASRs on baseline-aligned models (Table 1, starred cells) bear on V4. TSC-GRPO and Constrained SFT are deepening-style defenses tested against fine-tuning attacks and jailbreaks, bearing on V7. The central contribution is a new representation-level defense, so the study is T2 overall.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors claim semantic representation decay is the mechanistic cause of shallow alignment, but the evidence is a single-model probe/PCA experiment. They conclude that TSC-GRPO gives the lowest ASR under almost every jailbreak and resists fine-tuning attacks (average 2.8% ASR) without utility loss.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes a new causal-probe and GRPO training framework with cumulative causal penalties. It also evaluates harmful-example fine-tuning attacks, but does not report the original aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports ASR sensitivity to the uniformity weight λ, causal reward coefficient α, similarity threshold τ, and probe data-view construction; the discussion identifies λ=0.8, α=0.9, and τ=0.2 as optimal points in the displayed analyses.

fits_no_version.finding: A linear probe trained on final-layer hidden states at the end of the query drops from over 98% to near chance accuracy after a 'Sure, here is' prefix is forced.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In LLaMA-2-7B-Chat, linear separability of harmful vs safe intent in hidden states collapses once a compliant prefix is appended.

record.problems: The motivating probe result is reported mainly through Figure 1 and prose, without uncertainty estimates or a direct harmful-completion rate. The detailed Table 1 extraction is ambiguous, and the authors' aggregate attack summary does not identify which individual models have zero ASR for each named attack.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1's detailed per-model, per-attack cells are left out because the extracted layout does not confidently map all values to attack columns; the paper's explicit summary is recorded in r11. Identity-shifting attack results are also left out because that fine-tuning is designed to induce affirmative compliance and does not match the harmful-example or benign-data versions.

untested.parts: Only LLaMA-2-7B-Chat with 100 harmful pairs (plus a triggered backdoor). No range of example counts or other models.
Entirely untested; no per-token KL between aligned and base models. The probe-decay result measures a different construct.
Decoding changes are not tested. Suffix and other jailbreak numbers for baseline models are cited from prior papers, not reproduced. No no-attack ASR on AdvBench is given for the Table 1 baselines.
Untested. Semantic representation decay is proposed as a mechanism, but data or objective causes are not tested.

Whether TSC-GRPO actually spreads safety across later token positions (e.g. per-position KL or refusal recovery by depth) is not measured. The model was trained on prefix-forced data, so prefix robustness is partly in-distribution.

missing.what: Reproduced prefill ASR for baseline-aligned models: LLaMA-2-7B RLHF 27.1, LLaMA-3.1 SFT 51.24, NemoGuard 26.42, PSR 0.26; Qwen2.5-7B SFT 25.62, Egida-DPO 14.68, PSR 1.86; Qwen2.5-14B SFT 11.35, ShieldGemma 4.51, PSA 2.32, PSR 0.00; TSC-GRPO 0.00 throughout. Column mapping is inferred from the starred cells.

Identity-shifting fine-tuning attack on LLaMA-2-7B-Chat: Initial 0.0, Standard SFT 79.5, Constrained SFT 8.1, TSC-GRPO 0.0. Excluding it from V1 is reasonable, but it is a valid test of whether the defenses hold.
Utility before and after TSC-GRPO is roughly unchanged across four models (e.g. LLaMA-2 GSM8K 32.3 to 32.1), bearing on the cost of deepening.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked defense conditions to V1 (limits_scope) and defended models to V4 (challenges). Both are mislinks: defended models bear on V7, not on whether the attacks work on ordinary aligned models. Table 1 mixes values cited from other papers (unstarred) with reproduced ones (starred). Only the starred, apparently Prefill, column is the study's own evidence. The section 6.1 text says six models but lists four. Constrained SFT comes from an original source (2406.05946), but this study is not an original, so V7 verdicts are allowed.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests harmful-example fine-tuning on LLaMA-2-7B-Chat, including a backdoor condition; it does not test a broad range of harmful-example counts or models for this attack.
Ordinary or carefully chosen benign fine-tuning raising harmful compliance is not tested.
No per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models is reported.
The reported attack results concern named jailbreak attacks, including prefix injection; decoding changes are not tested.
The study does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
The study proposes semantic representation decay as a mechanism, but does not test whether the data or training objective caused the original shallowness.

TSC-GRPO is evaluated against jailbreak and fine-tuning attacks, but the study does not directly measure whether safety is distributed across more response-token positions, nor test other deepening methods.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7b-chat
rows.operation_detail: Train a linear probe at t=0 to classify harmful versus safe query hidden states, then evaluate it during forced compliant-prefix generation.
rows.measure: Linear-probe classification accuracy over generation time
rows.baseline: Chance level 0.5; probe accuracy at t=0 is reported as >98%
rows.value: After prefix injection, accuracy plummets to 0.5; Figure 1 describes it as remaining slightly above chance in subsequent generation.
rows.note: This is a probe-accuracy result, not a per-token KL measurement or harmful-completion rate; it is therefore not assigned to V3 or V4.

rows.subject: TSC-GRPO fine-tuned open-source LLMs (aggregate in the reported prose)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate attack success rates under jailbreak methods, including prefix injection; train with TSC-GRPO to support late-stage refusals.

conditions.value: The prose names AutoDAN, Prefix Injection, and ICA among the strong attacks
The prose does not specify which individual models attain zero for each named attack

rows.value: The authors report that TSC-GRPO often reduces ASR to zero for AutoDAN, Prefix Injection, and ICA, and has the lowest ASR under almost every attack method.
rows.note: The paper's prose gives this summary; detailed Table 1 cell-to-column assignments are omitted here because the extracted table layout is ambiguous.
rows.check: The subjects are TSC-GRPO-defended models, so this row cannot bear on V4, which concerns ordinary aligned models being bypassed. It bears on V7 only. Table 1 shows TSC-GRPO is not near zero on every attack (e.g. LLaMA-3.1 GCG 17.94, CodeCha. 24.48, DeepInc. 24.49). Unstarred Table 1 values are cited from other papers and should not be rows.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: TSC-GRPO and Constrained SFT on LLaMA-2-7B-Chat under the harmful-example attack and the untriggered backdoor
source_check.reason: Rows r3 and r4 report 4.6% and 1.8% ASR versus 88.9% under Standard SFT. Rows r7 and r9 report 1.9% and 1.6% without the backdoor trigger; the matched Standard SFT comparator is 7.6%, rather than 88.9%.

relationships.condition: Triggered backdoor fine-tuning, and some jailbreak families on TSC-GRPO models
relationships.reason: Some safety is lost under the triggered backdoor (10.9% Constrained SFT, 6.5% TSC-GRPO, vs 1.7% initial; r8, r10). In Table 1, TSC-GRPO ASR stays around 17–25% for GCG, CodeChameleon and DeepInception on some models (r11).
relationships.display_finding: Under the triggered backdoor, attack success rose to 10.9% for constrained SFT and 6.5% for TSC-GRPO against 1.7% initially, and TSC-GRPO stayed around 17–25% for GCG, CodeChameleon and DeepInception on some models.

source_check.condition: Triggered backdoor fine-tuning, and some jailbreak families on TSC-GRPO models
source_check.reason: Rows r8 and r10 retain 10.9% and 6.5% triggered ASR versus 1.7% initially. Table 1 additionally reports residual TSC-GRPO ASRs including 17.94% for GCG and 24.48% for CodeChameleon on LLaMA-3.1-8B, qualifying the robustness summarized by r11.

tranche.reason: The study tests safety deepening through a different method: a causal intent probe and GRPO with cumulative token-level penalties, evaluated against jailbreaks and harmful fine-tuning.
